target_customer: Startups that sell AI agents and need to run many of them in isolated persistent environments
problem: Running thousands of agents each with its own persistent computer requires infrastructure, scaling and monitoring work. Maritime manages that for $1 per agent per month.
business_model: usage-based hosting, $1 per month per 2 GB agent machine, per second billing for sandboxes
product_category: managed cloud infrastructure for AI agents

founders.name: Aryaman Shrivastava
prior_employers: MIT NANDA Lab (researcher, AI agent coordination at scale)

competitors.name: OpenComputer (DiggerHQ)
competitors.what: Persistent Linux VMs with hibernate and wake and checkpoints for agents
competitors.traction_then: launched July 25, 2026, priced from 0.004 dollars per minute

competitors.name: Anthropic Claude Managed Agents
competitors.what: Composable APIs to deploy cloud hosted agents

competitors.name: Microsoft Foundry hosted agents
competitors.what: Each agent session gets a VM isolated sandbox with persistent file system

technical_complexity.rationale: Isolated micro-VMs with persistence, sleep and wake, scaling and Windows and Android desktops are standard infrastructure engineering with some hard parts, built by a team of three.

defensibility.rationale: Large clouds and funded sandbox vendors sell the same primitive, and low price is the main wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large vendors launched managed agent hosting in 2026, before and around the batch.

market_need_then: Growth of AI agent startups in 2026 creates demand for per agent compute. The company gives no demand figures, and it lists use cases such as coding, evals and computer-use agents.

branding.domain_note: Uses maritime.sh, a .sh domain, not a .com.

identity.logo: not described by any source seen
identity.visual_style: practical, spec heavy site written partly as a briefing for AI agents
identity.voice_and_tone: direct and practical, ending with Get yours a computer today

branding.brand_signature: A page written as a briefing for AI agents
branding.community_and_virality: A Product Hunt post under the CEO's name invited beta users, with no engagement data seen.

brand_strength.rationale: Search for maritime brand results returns many unrelated shipping companies, so the name is generic and hard to find, though the product site is clear.

outcome_analysis: Maritime is a Fall 2026 company with no public outcome. It sells a low priced managed hosting product for AI agents with research backed founders from MIT NANDA, but it enters a market where large cloud vendors and a funded startup launched similar persistent agent computers within months. A generic name also makes search discovery harder.
notes: Dealroom lists 125k dollars at seed with a September 2026 founding date and names only Shrivastava as founder in one result, and I found no second source, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. Education was not found for either founder. DigitalOcean managed agents and other items dated after the batch are excluded from competition. Completeness pass: one seed round of 125K USD recorded from a single database (Dealroom, no round date or investors given). Everydev reports other figures (500K YC seed, a June 2026 pre-seed led by Two Lanterns Venture Capital) that are not confirmed elsewhere and not recorded.
